statement: You are given a binary array nums and an integer k.
You may flip at most k of the 0s to 1s. Return the length of the longest run of consecutive 1s you can end up with.
Equivalently, find the longest subarray that contains at most k zeros. Grow a window to the right, and whenever it holds more than k zeros, move its left edge forward until it holds k again.

examples.explanation: Flipping the zeros at indices 4 and 5 joins them to the four 1s that follow, giving 1s from index 4 to 9: six in a row.
Indices 2 to 11 contain exactly three zeros (at 4, 5 and 9). Flipping them gives a run of 10 ones, and no window holding at most three zeros is longer.
